g.title: n4
g.text: Transforms intake signals (food, water, substances) into physiological ingestion and absorption signals

g.title: n11
g.text: Represents path from nose to trachea.Transforms environmental gas signals into chemical levels and lung input for circulation

g.title: n17
g.text: Turns voiding commands into excretion intent

g.title: n23
g.text: Turns eating, drinking and smoking commands into ingestion metered over time

g.title: n28
g.text: Turns emotional stimuli into a decaying mental load

g.title: n33
g.text: Turns physical activity commands into a sustained metabolic load

g.title: n43
g.text: Blood system tracking O2 and CO2 levels

g.title: n56
g.text: GI tract: holds swallowed food and water, absorbing them into the body over time

g.title: n67
g.text: Muscular system: accrues fatigue under exertion, recovers at rest

g.title: n74
g.text: Skin: loses water, sweats when hot, and couples the body to ambient temperature and sun

g.title: n89
g.text: Systemic circulation: stroke volume, cardiac output and arterial pressure

g.title: n101
g.text: Adrenal glands: adrenaline in seconds, cortisol over minutes

g.title: n142
g.text: Kidney: sheds or conserves water according to hydration, and fills the bladder

g.title: n155
g.text: Liver: releases and stores glucose as the pancreas directs

g.title: n196
g.text: Pancreatic islets: insulin above the setpoint, glucagon below it

g.title: n204
g.text: Interprets physiological state as named feelings (hungry, thirsty, exhausted...)

g.title: n222
g.text: Observable state of the human being (e.g., temperature, blood pressure etc)

g.title: n313
g.text: Turns out-of-range reservoirs into organ damage (the death cascade)

g.title: n328
g.text: Internal physiological state (hydration, glycemia, energy, core temperature)
